blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: The quality of smartphone portrait photography has become increasingly important to both manufacturers and users. Recent devices use complex computational pipelines to improve facial rendering under varied lighting. These pipelines vary widely across manufacturers, so the same portrait can look noticeably different across smartphones. These differences affect multiple aspects of facial appearance, making perceptual preference difficult to characterize with a single measure. To address this, we propose an interpretable framework that decomposes face contrast into three components: overall facial tonal separation, eye-region contrast, and micro-contrast of fine skin details. We formulate dedicated metrics for each component and validate them via pairwise human judgments, demonstrating that our approach correlates more closely with human contrast perception than traditional contrast measures. To support this analysis, we introduce a realistic mannequin-based dataset designed for systematic facial contrast evaluation, comprising 508 full-resolution captures from 29 smartphones under diverse lighting, with region-specific masks and extensive pairwise perceptual annotations. As a downstream analysis, we show that combining the three component-wise metrics provides a meaningful basis for modeling balanced facial contrast preference in a controlled setting, and we present a preliminary evaluation on a smaller real-portrait dataset indicating that insights derived from the mannequin study can extend to real images. Our work provides a controlled first step toward defining and evaluating face contrast in portrait imaging.
blocks.zh: 智能手机肖像摄影的质量对制造商和用户都变得日益重要. 近期设备使用复杂的计算管道来改善不同照明下的脸部渲染. 这些管道在制造商之间差异很大,因此同样的肖像在智能手机之间可以看起来明显不同. 这些差异会影响面部外观的多方面,使得知觉偏好难以以单一度量法来定性. 为了解决这个问题,我们提出了一个可解释的框架,将面部对比分解为三个部分:整体面部内脏分裂,眼-区域对比,以及细细的皮肤细节的微缩相接. 我们为每个组成部分制定专门的衡量标准,并通过对人判断加以验证,表明我们的方法与人类的对比感比传统的对比度衡量方法更为相关。 为了支持这一分析,我们引入了一套基于人脸的实事求是的数据集,用于系统进行面相对比评价,包括29个智能手机在多种照明下508个全分辨率捕获,并配有区域特异性口罩和广泛的双相感知说明. 作为下游的分析,我们显示,结合三个分量度,为在受控环境下模拟平衡面部对比偏好提供了有意义的基础,我们提出对更小的真相数据集的初步评价,表明从人造人研究中获得的洞察力可以延伸到真实图像. 我们的工作为在肖像成像中界定和评价相貌对比提供了有控制的第一步。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
With the recent growth of smartphone photography, portrait imaging has become an increasingly important application. Modern devices rely on complex Image Signal Processing (ISP) pipelines to improve facial rendering under a wide range of lighting conditions [ 14 , 7 ] . These pipelines combine operations such as multi-frame fusion, tone mapping, denoising, sharpening, and face-specific enhancement, and they vary widely across manufacturers [ 14 , 42 , 40 ] .
As a result, the same portrait can appear noticeably different across devices, while the underlying processing remains largely a black box.
These differences are further accentuated in portrait photography, where humans are particularly apt at distinguishing subtle differences in faces [ 63 , 36 , 24 ] .
Together, these processing and perceptual factors make portrait quality difficult to explain with a single perceptual factor. Instead, multiple attributes such as exposure, detail preservation, noise, and local enhancement are all crucial [ 7 , 12 , 56 ] .
One particularly important attribute is face contrast. It influences dynamic range, mid-tone rendering, local contrast, and fine-detail visibility across the face. In practice, variations in face contrast can change the apparent depth of the face, the clarity of the eyes, and the visibility of the skin texture, even when the overall content of the scene remains the same, as illustrated in Figure 1 and 2 . Yet face contrast remains underexplored as a standalone perceptual attribute. Prior work has examined specific portrait quality factors, such as noise and texture [ 7 , 12 ] , but has not isolated face contrast itself as a distinct target of analysis.
This partially stems from the complex evaluation of face contrast in photography. Whereas general contrast measures are well studied [ 37 ] , face contrast does not have a single widely accepted definition.
Existing work on facial contrast [ 59 , 54 , 58 ] has mostly focused on feature-to-skin luminance or color differences, which do not fully capture how contrast is rendered in photographic portraits. Moreover, the appearance of face contrast is strongly affected by imaging conditions and processing, including illumination, tone reproduction, presence of flare and veil, local enhancement, and texture rendering [ 48 , 18 ] . As a result, face contrast has mostly been studied under idealized conditions, limiting its generalization across diverse lighting and smartphone rendering conditions.

blocks.en:
Existing approaches do not fully address this gap. General natural image quality assessment methods mainly target global perceptual quality [ 71 , 31 , 25 ] , whereas works related to face image quality [ 3 , 26 ] are often primarily designed for recognition utility rather than to understand how facial appearance is rendered. Our goal is different: rather than predicting global portrait quality or selecting the more preferred rendering, we aim to define and quantify the perceived amount of face contrast in a way that is interpretable and directly tied to portrait rendering. In this work, we propose to decompose face contrast into three perceptual components: overall contrast , eye contrast , and micro-contrast . Overall contrast captures coarse tonal separation across the face. Eye contrast is similar, but treated separately due to the importance of eyes in face perception [ 50 , 57 ] . Finally, micro-contrast captures the visibility of fine facial details in skin regions, focusing on how texture is rendered in the final portrait image rather than on intrinsic skin texture alone. The three components are intended to characterize the perceived amount of contrast in different facial regions and spatial scales.
Since more contrast is not necessarily better, we further consider balanced contrast, a holistic preference judgment over the relative balance of these components. This downstream analysis examines how the three component-wise measures relate to contrast preference in the controlled mannequin setting. To study these component-wise contrast measures under controlled variations, we build on prior mannequin-based studies of portrait texture quality [ 45 , 65 ] and use realistic mannequins to compare facial contrast across devices and lighting conditions. The main contributions of this paper are as follows:

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Previous work related to our study includes general image quality assessment, portrait quality assessment, face image quality for recognition, and classical contrast modeling. General image quality assessment (IQA) methods aim to predict overall perceptual image quality, either with reference images [ 68 , 33 , 34 , 78 ] or in a no-reference setting. In the no-reference setting, early hand-crafted models rely on natural-scene statistics [ 39 , 38 ] , while more recent approaches [ 5 , 79 , 62 , 72 , 71 , 31 , 25 , 67 , 2 , 10 ] are learning-based. These learning-based approaches are typically trained on human-rated image-quality datasets [ 60 , 53 , 52 ] . More recently, multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) based IQA methods use quality-aware prompting and scoring with vision-language representations [ 30 , 70 , 73 , 74 ] . These methods model global perceptual quality from image content and distortion patterns, but they are not designed to isolate face contrast as a specific perceptual attribute.
Portrait quality assessment methods [ 7 , 9 , 8 , 56 ] study portrait-specific attributes such as preservation of face detail, exposure, naturalness, noise, and global portrait quality. A related line of work studies face image quality for recognition [ 22 , 26 , 4 , 3 , 6 ] , where the goal is to estimate whether an image is suitable for matching or verification. While both directions are relevant, neither is primarily intended to evaluate face contrast itself.

以前与我们的研究有关的工作包括:一般图像质量评估、肖像质量评估、面相图像质量用于识别,以及古典对比模型制作。 一般图像质量评估方法旨在预测整体的能见度图像质量,有的采用参考图像[68,33,34,78],有的采用无参考环境. 在无参考设定中,早期手工制作的模型依赖于自然地貌统计[39,38],而更近期的方法[5,79,62,72,71,31,25,67,2,10]则是以学习为基础的. 这些以学习为基础的方法一般都接受关于人评级图像质量数据集的培训[60、53、52]。 最近,基于IQA的多式大语言模型(MLLMs)方法使用质量感知的提示和以视觉语言表示的评分[30、70、73、74]。 这些方法从图像内容和扭曲图案中模拟出全球认知质量,但它们的设计并不是将面相对比作为特定认知属性隔离出.
肖像质量评估方法[7,9,8,56]研究肖像特征,如保存相貌细节,曝光,自然,噪声,以及全球肖像质量等. 相关的一行工作研究面对图像质量以进行识别[22,26,4,3,6],目标是估计一个图像是否适合匹配或验证. 虽然两个方向都相关,但两者都并非主要旨在评价面相对比本身。

blocks.en: Contrast has long been studied in imaging, and classical measures such as Michelson contrast, Weber contrast, and RMS contrast remain widely used [ 37 , 43 , 55 ] . These formulations are well established for controlled stimuli, simple image patterns, and global image statistics. Previous work has also shown that contrast becomes harder to define for complex images, where perception depends on spatial structure and local image content [ 48 ] . This limitation is especially relevant for portraits, where perceived facial contrast depends not only on overall luminance range but also on the spatial distribution of tonal variation and the visibility of fine details. There have also been attempts to define facial contrast more explicitly in color science, cosmetics, and face perception [ 59 , 54 , 58 ] . In this literature, facial contrast is defined as the luminance or color difference between facial features, such as the eyes, lips, or eyebrows, and the surrounding skin, often through adapted Michelson formulations. Although these definitions are a starting point for our study, they present limitations when exploring portrait photos taken with various smartphones under different lighting conditions. Unfortunately, this ideal lighting scenario is not consistent with the way consumers take portraits, prompting the definition of more robust metrics.

blocks.en: 3 Contrast Definition
blocks.zh: 3 对照定义

blocks.en:
We define face contrast as a multi-scale perceptual property that cannot be fully captured by a single global statistic. We thus decompose it into three complementary components: overall contrast, eye contrast, and micro-contrast. This decomposition was developed through consultations with professional photographers to provide meaningful compositions that can vary independently. It also provides a practical and interpretable framework for face contrast analysis.
Figure 2 illustrates the diversity of facial contrast. Although images (a) and (b) were captured under the same lighting condition, they differ markedly because of device-specific face rendering: (a) shows high contrast from cast shadows, whereas (b) exhibits overly harsh skin texture. By contrast, image (c) shows high eye contrast with smooth skin. This diversity reinforces that contrast is an inherently complex attribute and further motivates the decomposition into three components.

blocks.en: • Overall contrast describes the global tonal separation across the face, reflecting how clearly bright and dark are separated [ 37 , 11 ] . • Eye contrast captures the local luminance separation within the eye region, which is semantically and visually critical in portrait perception [ 50 , 57 ] . • Micro-contrast quantifies the visibility of fine facial details, such as pores in the skin and small local structures [ 7 , 12 ] . • Balanced contrast describes the perceived harmony among different aspects of facial contrast. It reflects whether global tonal separation, eye definition, and fine-detail visibility are rendered in a natural and visually pleasing balance.

blocks.en: 4 Dataset construction
blocks.zh: 4 数据集构建

blocks.en:
We construct a portrait dataset using industry-grade realistic mannequins in a laboratory setup with controlled illumination, scene geometry, and camera motion. The complete dataset contains 508 full-resolution images acquired with 29 smartphones from multiple manufacturers under four illumination conditions (Figure 1 ).
For perceptual annotation, we supplement the original captures with DxO PhotoLab9 edits that increase or decrease tonal or micro-contrast. This yields 800 images with 2,400 region-specific masks (Fig. 3 ) [ 76 ] . Region-specific masks allow each contrast metric to be computed in its corresponding perceptually relevant region, while reducing interference from other components. The dataset uses two high-fidelity mannequins with different skin tones, Eugene and Diana, which reliably trigger the portrait rendering pipelines of the tested smartphones. Additional details on the mannequins, including materials and reflectance measurements, are provided in the supplementary material (Sec. A.3).
The images are organized into five groups based on lighting conditions, as shown in Table 1 . Groups 1–4 correspond to four distinct lighting conditions, while Group 5 combines non-overlapping samples from these conditions. Each of Groups 1–4 contains 75 images per mannequin, while Group 5 contains 100 images per mannequin.

blocks.en: 4.1 Annotation Protocol and JOD Scaling
blocks.zh: 4.1 注释协议和联合数据交换放大

blocks.en:
To align the proposed metrics with perception, we collect pairwise human judgments for each contrast component separately. Each pair is formed from images of the same mannequin identity, keeping facial structure and surface texture fixed across the two images so that observers can focus on differences in photographic rendering rather than differences between subjects. This setup also supports device-wise analysis of contrast rendering, reported in the supplementary material (Sec. F.4). Pairwise judgments allow for more precise annotations than ambiguous absolute scoring [ 80 ] .
During each annotation, explicit guidelines are provided so that contrast is assessed separately from preference, sharpness, or general image quality. (see the supplementary material Sec. C).
The annotation questions are phrased to match each target contrast attribute: 1. Overall contrast: “Which image has the larger range from darks to highlights?” 2. Eye contrast: “Choose the image with the darker pupil and brighter sclera (white of the eye).” 3. Micro-contrast: “Choose the image where the tiny details on the skin surface are more visible.” 4. Balanced contrast: “Which image has more balanced face contrast?” These task-specific prompts help to disentangle the three contrast components and encourage consistent perceptual judgments among observers. Balanced contrast is collected as a separate annotation task and is used only for the downstream preference analysis, not to define the three contrast components. Across all four tasks, trained image-quality experts completed 20,000 pairwise comparisons over 160 hours in total. To improve annotation efficiency, image pairs are sampled using an active pairwise comparison strategy [ 20 ] , so that the collected comparisons focus on informative pairs rather than exhaustively enumerating all possible combinations. For each contrast task, pairwise choices are converted into interval-scale values in Just Objectionable Difference (JOD) units using a Thurstone Case V paired-comparison model. A difference of 1 JOD between two images means that 75% of observers would vote for the image with the higher JOD value [ 49 ] . The JOD scale is estimated independently for each mannequin and comparison set. For Groups 1–4, a separate scale is estimated for each lighting condition, whereas Group 5 uses a single mixed-lighting scale per mannequin.

blocks.en:
We propose metrics for the three face-contrast components defined above: overall contrast, eye contrast, and micro-contrast. These interpretable, perceptually grounded measures are evaluated against human annotations in the following section.
Following prior work on facial contrast [ 59 , 54 , 58 ] , we analyze facial lightness in the CIELAB color space. Specifically, we use the L ∗ L^{*} channel and normalize it to [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] , which provides an approximately perceptual lightness representation while separating tonal variation from chromatic variation. We denote by L L the normalized lightness image, and Ω f \Omega_{f} , Ω e \Omega_{e} , and Ω s \Omega_{s} denote the face, eye, and skin masks, respectively.

The eyes are structurally distinct from the rest of the face because they contain both very dark regions (pupil) and very bright ones (sclera). Their contrast is therefore not always well captured by global facial contrast alone. Previous work on face perception [ 50 , 57 ] also supports treating the eye region as a separate component of face contrast due to its singular role in face recognition. In addition, directional lighting can also strongly affect the separation between the pupil, iris, and sclera, making the eyes appear flatter or grayer. We thus treat eye contrast as a separate component and measure it from
the dominant dark–bright separation within the eye region. We divide the luminance values within the eye mask Ω e \Omega_{e} into two classes using the Otsu thresholding method [ 47 ] . The left-and right-eye masks are merged before applying a single Otsu threshold.
Let D D and B B denote the resulting dark and bright pixel sets, respectively. We define eye contrast as C eye = μ B − μ D , C_{\mathrm{eye}}=\mu_{B}-\mu_{D}, (3) where μ B \mu_{B} and μ D \mu_{D} are the mean lightness values of the bright and dark classes.

blocks.en: 5.3 Micro-Contrast ( C micro C_{\mathrm{micro}} )
blocks.zh: 5.3 微型连锁店(C-micro C-_{\mathrm{micro}}-)

blocks.en:
Micro-contrast is intended to capture the visibility of fine-scale facial texture in skin regions while remaining relatively insensitive to broader shading and illumination. In photography, micro-contrast is a commonly used but imprecise term, sometimes used interchangeably with texture visibility [ 69 , 21 ] . Here, we use it more specifically to describe the extent to which fine facial details are rendered in the final portrait image,
distinguishing it from a general preference for stronger sharpening or texture enhancement. As micro-contrast depends on both surface texture and the camera pipeline, our controlled mannequin setup fixes the underlying facial texture within each identity. This allows us to isolate how different devices render the same fine-scale details.
We now describe each stage of the proposed C micro C_{\mathrm{micro}} computation.

blocks.en:
We evaluate the proposed methods under two complementary settings. (i) Within-lighting evaluation is conducted separately for Groups 1–4 using a device-disjoint train/validation split comprising 19 training devices and 10 validation devices. It measures generalization to unseen devices within a fixed lighting condition. The complete device allocation is reported in the supplementary material (Sec. F.2).
(ii) Mixed-lighting evaluation is conducted on Group 5, which contains images from multiple lighting conditions that do not overlap with Groups 1–4 and are assessed on a common JOD scale. For fitted balanced contrast preference predictors, Groups 1–4 are used for parameter estimation and Group 5 is used exclusively for evaluation.
We evaluate the Overall, Eye, and Micro contrast measures by computing Pearson’s linear correlation coefficient (PLCC) and
Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient (SRCC) against their corresponding component-specific JOD scores, as reported in Table 2 . For balanced-contrast preference, the three contrast components are instead jointly fitted to predict balanced-contrast JOD, with results reported in Table 3 .

blocks.en: Overall Contrast. We compare the proposed metric with classical luminance statistics and prior facial contrast measures [ 59 , 54 , 58 ] . It achieves the highest nominal correlations, with PLCC/SRCC of 0.792/0.780 for within-lighting and 0.688/0.693 for mixed-lighting evaluation . Global luminance measures are competitive within lighting but degrade under mixed lighting. Feature-to-skin measures show weaker correlations, as they quantify luminance or chromatic differences between facial features and the surrounding skin rather than face-wide shading and tonal variation. These results suggest that overall facial contrast depends on the spatial distribution of relative tonal variation across the face.

blocks.en:
As a downstream analysis, we examine whether the three proposed contrast components provide a useful basis for modeling balanced contrast preference. In this task, annotators selected the image with the most balanced contrast , reflecting an overall judgment rather than any single component in isolation.
Our best variant is a second-order polynomial regressor over the three proposed contrast components (see supplementary Sec D.6).
As shown in Table 3 , this model reaches PLCC/SRCC values of 0.728/0.739 under within-lighting and 0.773/0.778 under mixed-lighting .
Each component alone yields non-trivial but suboptimal performance, indicating that balanced contrast preference is not explained by a single attribute. We further compare against five related families: hand-crafted IQA [ 39 , 38 ] , general IQA [ 2 , 67 , 62 , 71 , 25 , 10 ] , MLLM-based IQA [ 70 , 73 , 30 ] , portrait IQA [ 9 ] , and face-quality assessment [ 6 , 3 , 26 , 4 , 22 ] . The IQA methods primarily target global perceptual image quality, whereas portrait IQA focuses on portrait quality. Face-quality models assess facial image quality, often in the context of biometric utility or recognition-related tasks.
We evaluate both off-the-shelf and after lightweight task adaptation to balanced contrast preference.
Before adaptation, most learning-based methods perform markedly worse, indicating a gap between their original objectives and balanced contrast assessment. MLLM-based IQA models show relatively strong zero-shot performance. Given the limited training data, we evaluate these large models zero-shot to avoid unreliable adaptation.

在适应之前,大多数以学习为基础的方法都表现得更糟糕,表明其原始目标与均衡对比评估之间存在差距。 基于MLLM的IQA模型显示相对强大的零发性能. 鉴于培训数据有限,我们对这些大型模型进行零镜头评估,以避免不可靠的适应.

blocks.en:
For a fairer comparison, we fine-tune remaining learned baselines using lightweight trainable heads while keeping the pretrained representation largely frozen. After adaptation, performance improves substantially for several learned baselines, especially face-quality models.
Among all methods, fine-tuned IFQA [ 22 ] achieves the highest performance. IFQA was pretrained using human preference judgments of restored faces, which may make its representation particularly suitable for this task. Nevertheless, our proposed component-based model remains the strongest among learning-free methods and the second-best method overall.
Combining our metrics surpasses most neural-network-based baselines, showing that the proposed decomposition captures a substantial part of balanced contrast preference in the controlled setting. The remaining gap to fine-tuned IFQA suggests that balanced contrast judgments may also depend on additional cues beyond the three explicit contrast components.
This latter aspect is where neural-network approaches shine: using large amounts of pretraining data, they are able to efficiently model human preference. While our method performs best in low-data regimes or when interpretability is desired, learning-based approaches can be used to capture the remaining subtlety in human contrast preferences. We expect the interaction between the two paradigms to yield improved models of contrast preference.

为了进行更公平的比较,我们利用轻量级的可训练头来微调剩余的知识基线,同时使训练前的表述基本被冻结。 适应后,一些学到的基线,特别是面部质量模型的性能大有改进。
在所有方法中,经过微调的IFQA[22]实现最高性能. 《质量法》通过人对恢复面孔的偏好判断进行预先培训,这可能使其代表性特别适合这项任务。 然而,我们提议的基于组成部分的模式仍然是无学习方法中最强的,是总体第二好的方法。
结合我们的度量衡超过了大多数基于神经网络的基线,表明拟议的分解在所控制的环境下捕捉了相当一部分均衡的对比偏好. 对《国际质量评估》进行微调的剩余差距表明,平衡的对比判断还可能取决于三个明确对比部分以外的额外提示。
后一方面是神经-网络方法发光的地方:利用大量预训数据,它们能够高效地模拟人类偏好. 虽然我们的方法在低数据制度中或在期望可解释性时表现最好,但可以采用以学习为基础的方法来捕捉人类对比偏好中剩下的微妙之处。 我们期望两种模式之间的相互作用将产生更好的对比偏好模式。

blocks.en: 6.3 Generalization to Real Portrait Data
blocks.zh: 6.3 概论为真实外观数据

blocks.en:
To examine whether the mannequin-based findings extend to real portraits, we collected a smaller, less controlled dataset of 444 images from 10 subjects/scenes. It contains 29 unique capture devices, 18 of which are not present in the mannequin dataset. We generate contrast-adjusted variants using DxO PhotoLab 9 to obtain at least 44 images per scene for reliable pairwise comparison. It includes more varied facial appearances and poses, including three-quarter views (Supplementary Fig. S14). We collected pairwise annotations for overall contrast, eye contrast, and micro-contrast using the same questions as in the controlled study and converted them to JOD scores, requiring 80 annotation hours. We compare the proposed zero-shot metrics with IFQA fine-tuned on the mannequin annotations (Table 4 ). Our metrics outperform fine-tuned IFQA for eye and micro-contrast, while IFQA performs better for overall contrast. Without fitting on mannequin or real-portrait annotations, the proposed metrics retain meaningful correlations on real portraits. We additionally report scene-wise performance with uncertainty in Supplementary Table S9.
These results suggest that the mannequin dataset can bridge controlled contrast analysis and real-portrait evaluation.
Broader evaluation across identities, skin tones, poses, and capture conditions remains important future work.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We constructed a realistic mannequin-based dataset captured using multiple smartphones under diverse lighting conditions. For controlled face contrast evaluation, we paired the dataset with region-specific masks and psychophysical annotations. Rather than treating face contrast as a single global quantity, we decomposed it into three perceptual components: overall contrast, eye contrast, and micro-contrast, and proposed an interpretable metric for each attribute. The key improvement over previous metrics lies in leveraging the multi-scale and multi-frequency aspects of contrast perception.
Our experimental results demonstrate that the three proposed metrics align closely with human contrast perception, and perform strongly against conventional contrast, texture and sharpness measures.
These results suggest that face contrast in portrait imaging is better understood as a structured, multi-scale perceptual property rather than as a simple global statistic. As a downstream analysis, we examined the preference for balanced facial contrast in the controlled mannequin setting.
The measured overall, eye, and micro-contrast components provide a meaningful basis for explaining holistic contrast preference: each component alone is insufficient, while their combination explains substantially more variation in human judgments.
A fine-tuned face-quality model achieved slightly higher correlations, suggesting that balanced contrast judgments may be influenced by additional cues beyond the three explicit contrast components. We also evaluated the proposed metrics on real-world portraits, showing that our zero-shot metrics generalize beyond the controlled mannequin setting. We hope that the proposed dataset and interpretable formulation will support future work on interpretable portrait quality modeling and face-contrast evaluation.

我们用多种照明条件下的多台智能手机 构建了一个以人造人为主的数据集 为了进行控制面相对比评价,我们把数据集与特定区域的口罩和心理物理说明配对。 我们没有将相貌对比作为一个单一的全球量来对待,而是将其分解为三个感知成分:整体对比,相眼对比,和微相接,并针对每个属性提出了一个可解释的度量. 与以前的衡量标准相比,主要的改进在于利用对比感的多尺度和多频率方面。

这些结果表明,肖像成像中的相貌对比被更好的理解为一个有条理的多尺度的感知属性,而不是简单的全球统计. 作为下游的分析,我们研究了在受控的外观布局中 偏好平衡的面部对比。

一个精细的面部质量模型实现了略高的关联性,表明平衡的对比判断可能受三个明显对比部分以外的额外提示所影响. 我们还评价了关于现实世界肖像的拟议衡量标准,表明我们的零射入射度衡量标准超越了受控制的人造人设定。 我们希望,拟议的数据集和可解释的表述将支持今后关于可解释的肖像质量模型和相容评价的工作。

Intuitively, this procedure maps binary pairwise decisions onto a continuous perceptual axis. Images with similar JOD values are difficult to distinguish perceptually for the target attribute, whereas larger JOD differences correspond to stronger perceived differences. These JOD values are then used as perceptually grounded references for evaluating the proposed contrast metrics.
To quantify uncertainty in the recovered perceptual scale, we estimate confidence intervals using the analytical error-estimation framework of Zolliker and Barańczuk [ 81 ] . Because our annotation protocol uses active pairwise sampling, these intervals should be interpreted as approximate scale-level uncertainty estimates rather than exact finite-sample guarantees. We use them as a practical indicator of the stability of the recovered JOD values under the incomplete comparison design.

blocks.en: A.3 Controlled Portrait Test Bench
blocks.zh: A.3 受控外观试验台

blocks.en:
Figure S1 shows examples of images captured using a controlled portrait-imaging test bench. The setup is designed to ensure repeatable acquisition while reproducing realistic portrait scenes. It includes a realistic mannequin, a composite chart, a flare light source, a multispectral lighting system, a ColorChecker with grayscale patches, and an automated moving object. Together, these components allow us to vary facial appearance, illumination, flare, tonal and color references, and temporal scene conditions.
The use of a mannequin allows us to capture the same face repeatedly while avoiding variations in expression, pose, and subject motion. Its skin-like reflectance and fine surface details also make it suitable for evaluating how different smartphones render facial appearance under controlled conditions. The mannequins are realistic replicas of human subjects and are specifically designed for image-quality evaluation. They were tested to reliably trigger smartphone portrait modes. The mannequins are constructed from polyurethane foam with proprietary skin-like pigmentation, silicone components, real hair, and glass eyes. Figure S2 shows that the realistic mannequins closely follow the reflectance trends of the corresponding real human skin across the visible wavelength range.
The composite chart and the ColorChecker with grayscale patches provide reference structures for checking exposure and color consistency throughout the acquisition process. Illumination is controlled using a multispectral lighting system so that both the spectrum and intensity of the scene can be varied systematically. In this work, lux denotes the measured illuminance on the mannequin, while Δ ​ EV \Delta\mathrm{EV} denotes the calibrated exposure difference between the light on the mannequin and the light produced by the LED panel. Thus, lux controls the physical amount of ambient light reaching the setup, whereas Δ ​ EV \Delta\mathrm{EV} controls the relative strength of the LED backlight with respect to the mannequin illumination. By varying both factors, we obtain portrait images spanning flat and non-uniform lighting conditions, as well as a broad range of facial contrast appearances. A dedicated flare light source is used to introduce controlled stray-light and veiling-glare conditions, which can reduce tonal separation and affect perceived face contrast. Finally, the automated moving object introduces temporal variation into the scene, allowing the test bench to account for motion effects in multi-frame capture and ISP processing.

blocks.en: 1. Which image has more contrast? For this task, we make three separate annotations. Please note that we do not evaluate color contrast or texture contrast in the photographic sense. Here, color contrast refers to contrast created by differences in color, while texture contrast refers to contrast created by differences in surface texture. Instead, we focus only on tonal contrast for the overall contrast and eye-region contrast questions, and on micro-contrast for the skin-detail evaluation. Also, we are not choosing which image looks better. The goal is simply to decide which image has more contrast . blocks.en: B.1 Overall Contrast

blocks.en: In this task, annotators are shown whole-face masked images without any background. As shown in Figure S4 , they compare several face images taken under different illumination and exposure settings. When we talk about overall contrast, we mainly mean tonal contrast: the difference between the dark and bright parts of the face. Bright regions such as the sclera and dark regions such as the eye sockets naturally contribute to the overall tonal range of the face. This is especially important for dark-skinned mannequins, where the eyes may contain the strongest bright–dark separation. However, this task is distinct from the Eye-Region Contrast task: Overall Contrast measures global tonal separation across the whole face, whereas Eye-Region Contrast evaluates only the local tonal structure inside the eye region (e.g., sclera vs. iris vs. pupil).
blocks.zh: 在这个任务中,无任何背景的全面蒙面图像显示注释者. 如图S4所示,它们比较了在不同照明和曝光环境中拍摄的多张相片。 当我们谈论整体对比时,我们主要指的就是"内在对比":面部的阴暗和明亮部分的区别. 明亮的区域如斯克勒拉和暗区域如眼套等,自然有助于面部的整体直径. 这对深肤色的模特尤其重要,因为眼睛可能包含最强的亮相-暗相相。 然而,这一任务不同于眼界对比任务: 整体对比度测量整个面部的全局肾上腺分化,而Eye-Region对比度只评价眼部区域内的局部肾上腺结构(如sclera vs. iris vs. situal).

blocks.en: Lighting can strongly influence overall contrast. For example, in Figures 4(a) and 4(b) , strong directional lighting creates a clear separation between bright and dark areas, so these images have higher overall contrast. In contrast, the image in Figure 4(c) does not have strong lighting differences, so the contrast is more moderate and even. It is important to remember that we are not choosing the image that looks the most pleasing or natural. For example, Figure 4(c) may look the most pleasing overall, but our goal here is simply to decide which image has more contrast. Finally, in some cases, such as Figure 4(d) , the face may look flat because of flare or veiling light. This reduces the separation between bright and dark areas, so we consider it to have low overall contrast.

blocks.en:
In this task, annotators are shown only the eye masks, without any background.
When judging contrast in the eyes, consider the following: contrast is higher when the pupil appears darker and the white of the eye appears brighter. Sometimes, there may be small white reflections on the pupil caused by light. In such cases, a brighter reflection also contributes to a higher-contrast appearance. Please note that natural eye color, such as blue or brown, should not influence the decision. Eye color is not related to the contrast we want to measure.

blocks.en: B.3 Micro-Contrast
blocks.zh: B.3 微型通信公司

blocks.en: In this task, annotators are shown only the skin masks, without any background. The goal is to judge how clearly the small skin textures appear. Please focus on details such as pores, fine lines, and eyebrow or forehead texture. When these tiny details look sharper and more visible, the image has higher micro-contrast. When they look soft or blurred, the micro-contrast is lower. For the Eugene mannequin, the beard area may also be visible. If the beard texture appears clear, this also counts as higher micro-contrast. Please note that micro-contrast is not about color or lighting. For example, an image taken in a dark environment may look very noisy, making it hard to see the skin texture. In that case, even if the color or brightness is different, the micro-contrast should still be judged as low because the fine details are not visible.
blocks.zh: 在这一任务中,只显示护肤面具,没有任何背景. 目标是判断小皮肤纹理的出现有多清晰. 请集中关注毛孔,细线等细节,以及眉毛或前额纹理. 当这些细小的细节看起来更尖锐,更能被看到时,图像具有更高的微相通. 当它们看起来柔软或模糊时,微接层会更低. 对于"尤金活字"(Eugene mannequin)来说,胡子区域也可能是可见的. 如果胡子的纹理看起来清晰,这也算作更高的微相通. 请注意,微缩相接与颜色或照明无关. 例如,在黑暗环境中拍摄的图像可能看起来非常吵闹,使得人们很难看到皮肤的纹理. 在这种情况下,即使颜色或亮度不同,由于细细的细节不明显,微孔仍应评为低相.

blocks.en: Main question: “Can you clearly see the tiny details on the skin surface?” When evaluating micro-contrast, we are looking for local regions where we can see details and texture. High micro-contrast means that the texture looks very crisp. Low micro-contrast causes the skin to appear overly smooth, plastic, or softened. Note that higher micro-contrast does not mean that the image looks more pleasant.

blocks.en: C.4 Balanced Contrast Preference Guideline
blocks.zh: C.4 平衡对比优先准则

blocks.en: Main question: “Which image has more balanced contrast?” Balanced contrast refers to the image whose facial contrast appears most natural and visually well balanced overall. Annotators should consider whether the face has sufficient tonal separation without appearing too flat, too harsh, over-sharpened, or unnatural. Unlike the previous three tasks, this judgment is based on overall preference rather than the amount of a single contrast component.
blocks.zh: 主要问题: “哪一个形象有更平衡的对比?” 平衡对比指其面部对比看起来最自然,视觉上整体平衡的图像. 注释者应考虑面部是否具有足够的直肠分出而不显得过于平坦,过于苛刻,过度收缩,或不自然. 与前三项任务不同,这一判断是基于总体偏好,而不是单一对比成分的金额.

blocks.en: D.2 Overall Contrast Ablation Study
blocks.zh: D.2 总体对比性研究

blocks.en:
Table S1 examines the sensitivity of the proposed overall-contrast measure to the choice of spatial scales. We consider both leave-one-scale-out variants of the reference set, ℛ = { 16 , 32 , 64 , 128 , 256 } \mathcal{R}=\{16,32,64,128,256\} , and alternative scale sets obtained by shifting or densifying the sampled scales.
Removing either of the two finest scales (16 or 32 pixels) consistently decreases both PLCC and SRCC under the Within-lighting and Mixed-lighting evaluations. Removing the intermediate 64-pixel scale results in only a small change, whereas removing the two coarsest scales yields higher nominal correlations. In particular, excluding the 256-pixel scale gives the highest nominal correlations in the leave-one-scale-out analysis, reaching PLCC/SRCC values of 0.815 / 0.806 0.815/0.806 within lighting and 0.729 / 0.729 0.729/0.729 under mixed lighting, compared with 0.792 / 0.780 0.792/0.780 and 0.688 / 0.693 0.688/0.693 , respectively, for the reference configuration. The bootstrap distributions nevertheless exhibit substantial overlap, indicating that the observed differences should be interpreted as a tendency rather than a definitive advantage of a particular scale set.
blocks.zh:
表S1审查了拟议总体连续措施对空间尺度选择的敏感性。 我们认为,参考数据集R={16、32、64、128、256}的 " 留一尺度 " 的变体和通过转移或去化所抽样的尺度而获得的 " 备选尺度 " 。
在 " 照明内 " 和 " 混合照明评价 " 下,取消两个最优的尺度(16或32像素)中的任何一种都持续地减少PLCC和SRCC。 移除中间的64-像素尺度只产生小的改变,而去掉两个相近的尺度则产生较高的名义相关性. 特别是,不包括256像素平面图,在一号平面图解分析中给出了最高的名义相关性,在照明内达到0.815/0.806/0.815/0.806和0.729/0.729 在混合照明下,参考配置分别为0.792/0.780/0.792/0.780和0.688/0.693。 然而,靴子的分布有相当程度的重叠,表明观察到的差异应被解释为一种趋势,而不是某一套比例的绝对优势。

blocks.en:
A similar trend is observed when perturbing the complete scale set. Shifting all scales toward smaller spatial support yields moderately higher nominal correlations, while shifting them toward larger support reduces performance. Increasing the sampling density using half-octave spacing produces results close to the reference configuration, suggesting that the metric does not benefit substantially from a denser sampling of the same spatial range.
Overall, these results indicate that the proposed measure is reasonably robust to moderate changes in the scale set, while also suggesting that the coarsest spatial support may be less informative for the face crops considered in our dataset. We retain the originally specified R = 16 , 32 , 64 , 128 , 256 R={16,32,64,128,256} configuration in the main experiments to avoid retrospectively selecting the scale set based on the evaluation annotations, and report the present analysis as a sensitivity study rather than using it for post-hoc parameter tuning.

总的来说,这些结果表明,拟议措施相当有力,可以适度地改变比例,同时也表明,对数据集中考虑的面料作物而言,最短的空间支持可能信息较少。 我们保留了主要实验中最初指定的R=16,32,64,128,256R={16,32,64,128,256)的配置,以避免根据评价说明追溯性选择所设定的比分,并将本分析报告为敏感性研究,而不是用于后热参数调试.

blocks.en: D.3 Eye Contrast Ablation Study
blocks.zh: D.3. 眼相容症研究

blocks.en: As a simple baseline, eye-region contrast can be defined using a Michelson-style normalized range computed from percentile extrema within the eye mask: L min = P 1 ​ ( L eye ) , L max = P 99 ​ ( L eye ) , L_{\min}=P_{1}(L_{\mathrm{eye}}),\qquad L_{\max}=P_{99}(L_{\mathrm{eye}}), (6) and C eye = L max − L min L max + L min . C_{\mathrm{eye}}=\frac{L_{\max}-L_{\min}}{L_{\max}+L_{\min}}. (7) This formulation measures the separation between the darkest and brightest structures in the eye region and can provide a reasonable approximation when the pupil/iris and sclera are clearly separated.
blocks.zh: 作为简单的基线,可以使用Michelson式的正态范围来定义眼区对比: L min = P 1 (L eye),L max = P 99 (L eye),L _{\ min }= P_{ 1} (L _{\ mathrm{ eye}}),\qquad L_{\ max}= P_{99} (L _{\ mathrm{ eye}}), (L_{\ _{\ mathrm{ ye}}), (6)和 C 眼 = L 最大- L 最小- L 最大- L 最小- L 分钟。 (原始内容存档于2018-09-26) (中文(中国大陆) ). C_{\mathrm{ye}}=\frac{L_{\max}-L_{\min}}{L_{\max}+L_{\min}}. (7) 这种配方测量了眼区最黑暗和最明亮的结构之间的分出,在瞳孔/眼和眼窗明显分离时可以提供合理的近似值。

blocks.en: However, this normalized range becomes less reliable in low-contrast cases. When both the bright and dark structures are compressed into a narrow luminance range, the resulting score may no longer reflect the perceived separation between the pupil, iris, and sclera. As a result, the Michelson-style ordering can become perceptually unstable. Figure S11 illustrates such a failure case: although Image 212030 appears to have lower eye contrast than Image 212022, the Michelson [ 37 ] measure does not preserve this perceptual ordering.
blocks.zh: 然而,在低争议案件中,这种正常化范围变得不那么可靠。 当亮和暗两种结构被压缩成狭窄的亮度范围后,产生的分数可能不再反映瞳孔,虹膜和斯克勒拉之间的感知分出. 因此,Michelson式的订单可能会在概念上变得不稳定. 图S11说明了这样的故障情况:虽然图像212030似乎比图像212022有更低的眼睛对比,但Michelson [37] 度量法并没有保持这种感官顺序.

blocks.en: For this reason, we adopt the Otsu-based formulation in the main method. By partitioning the luminance values within the eye mask into dominant dark and bright classes, the proposed measure better reflects the perceptually meaningful separation between the darker pupil/iris region and the brighter sclera and highlights. Figure S12 further shows that even in a challenging low-contrast regime, the Otsu-based [ 47 ] formulation still yields a perceptually plausible ranking.
blocks.zh: 为此,我们采用以大津为主的方法。 通过将眼罩内的亮度值分入占优势的黑暗和明亮的阶层,拟议的衡量标准更好地反映了较暗的瞳孔/日光区域与更亮的斯克勒拉和亮度之间的感知性有意义的分离. 图S12还表明,即使在一个具有挑战性的低相冲突制度下,基于大津的[47]个配方仍能产生一种明显可信的排名。

blocks.en: Figure S11 : Face images and corresponding eye-region crops ordered by the Michelson eye-contrast measure [ 37 ] . blocks.en: D.6 Balanced Contrast Preference Ablation Study
blocks.zh: D.6 平衡对比偏好研究

blocks.en:
We compare three balanced contrast preference-model variants using the proposed contrast measures as predictors: a non-negative linear regressor, a second-order polynomial regressor, and a pairwise-trained MLP. The second-order polynomial augments the three contrast components with their squared and cross-component interaction terms.
The pairwise-trained MLP uses the same augmented representation and independently maps each image to a scalar balanced contrast score. It is trained using pairwise ranking supervision together with a balanced contrast JOD regression regularizer, following the training protocol described in the next subsection.
Table S5 compares the three variants under the within-lighting and mixed-lighting evaluations.
blocks.zh:
我们比较了三个均衡的对比偏好模型,将拟议的对比度作为预测器:一个非负线性递减器,一个二等多诺性递减器,和一个双相训练的MLP. 第二顺序多诺米亚语用其正方形和跨元件交互名词来增强三个相对分的元件.
双相训练的 MLP 使用相同的增强的表示并独立地将每个图像映射到一个平面平面对比分. 根据下一分节所述培训协议,通过双向排名监督以及平衡对比的JOD回归调节器对其进行培训。
表S5比较了内放光和混合放光评价下的三个变种.

blocks.en:
The two evaluations differ in how the balanced contrast preference predictors are fitted and evaluated. In the within-lighting evaluation, a separate model is fitted for each mannequin and each of Groups 1–4 using the corresponding device-disjoint training split, and evaluated on the held-out devices from the same group. Because the balanced contrast JOD scale is estimated independently for each group and mannequin, each model is fitted and evaluated within its corresponding JOD scale. In the mixed-lighting evaluation, a single model per mannequin is fitted using Groups 1–4 and evaluated on the held-out Group 5 without refitting or using its balanced contrast labels. For each mannequin, the training balanced contrast JOD values therefore originate from four independently estimated group-specific scales, whereas Group 5 provides a single mixed-lighting JOD scale.
Within-lighting results are computed separately for the eight Group–mannequin evaluation subsets and then macro-averaged. Mixed-lighting results are computed separately for Diana and Eugene on Group 5 and then macro-averaged over the two mannequins.
blocks.zh:
两种评价在平衡对比偏好预测器的配置和评价方面各不相同。 在照明内评价中,每名模特和每名第1至4组都安装一个单独的模型,使用相应的设备分解训练,并在同一组的被搁置装置上进行评估。 由于平衡对比的JOD比例表是针对每个组和人造人独立估计的,因此每个模型都在其相应的JOD比例表内被安装和评价. 在混合照明评价中,使用第1至第4组安装了每只人造人单一的模型,并在被搁置的第5组上加以评价,而无需重新配置或使用其平衡的对比标签。 因此,对每名模特来说,培训平衡对比的JOD值来源于四个独立估计的针对特定群体的尺度,而第5组则提供单一的混合照明的JOD尺度。
对8个小组的人力评价子集分别计算照明内结果,然后进行宏观平均计算。 第5组的戴安娜和尤金的混合照明结果分别计算,然后对两个人造人进行宏观平均计算。

blocks.en: As shown in Table S5 , the second-order polynomial regressor achieves the highest overall performance, reaching PLCC/SRCC values of 0.728 / 0.739 0.728/0.739 within lighting and 0.773 / 0.778 0.773/0.778 under mixed lighting. The pairwise-trained MLP is competitive but remains slightly below the polynomial model overall, while the non-negative linear regressor performs worse in both settings. We therefore use the second-order polynomial regressor in the main balanced contrast preference analysis, as it remains compact and explicitly parameterized while capturing quadratic effects and cross-component interactions.

blocks.en: Table S9 reports scene-wise PLCC/SRCC for overall contrast, eye contrast, and micro-contrast. For each attribute, we compare the proposed zero-shot metric with IFQA fine-tuned on the corresponding mannequin-based annotations. Correlations are computed separately for each scene and macro-averaged across the 10 scenes. The proposed metrics achieve average PLCC/SRCC values of 0.792/0.825 for overall contrast, 0.753/0.768 for eye contrast, and 0.717/0.731 for micro-contrast. For overall contrast, fine-tuned IFQA performs better on average, whereas the proposed metric remains competitive without training on either mannequin or real-portrait annotations. For eye contrast, the proposed metric achieves higher average PLCC and SRCC than fine-tuned IFQA. Performance varies across scenes for both approaches, reflecting the greater diversity of subjects and capture conditions in the real-portrait dataset.
blocks.zh: 表S9按场景报告PLCC/SRCC的总体对比度、相眼对比度和微相接度。 对于每个属性,我们比较了拟议的零射入度量衡和在相应的以人造人为主的注解上微调的IFQA. 每个场景的关联性分别计算,10个场景的宏观平均值分别计算. 拟议衡量标准的总对比值为:0.792/0.825;0.753/0.768;0.717/0.731。 相比之下,经过微调的《国际质量评估》平均表现较好,而拟议的衡量标准仍然具有竞争力,没有关于人造人或真实图说明的培训。 就眼对比而言,拟议的衡量标准比经过微调的IFQA实现更高的平均PLCC和SRCC. 两种方法的性能因场景不同而不同,反映了主体的更大多样性并捕捉了真相数据集中的条件.

blocks.en:
Table S10 further examines the effect of mannequin-based fine-tuning on IFQA. Without task-specific adaptation, IFQA yields negative average correlations with all three contrast attributes, indicating that its off-the-shelf quality scores are not directly aligned with the attribute-specific contrast judgments considered in this work. Fine-tuning on the corresponding mannequin-based annotations substantially improves performance across all three attributes. This distinction is important when interpreting the comparison with the proposed metrics: our metrics are applied directly to real portraits without fitting to either mannequin or real-portrait annotations, whereas IFQA benefits from task-specific supervision on the mannequin dataset. In particular, the improvement after fine-tuning, including the strong performance of IFQA for overall contrast, provides additional evidence that the controlled mannequin annotations capture contrast-related information that transfers to real portraits.
Overall, these results support the proposed mannequin dataset as a controlled bridge for studying photographic face contrast, while also showing that the proposed zero-shot metrics generalize meaningfully to real portrait images.
blocks.zh:
表S10还审查了以人马为主的微调对IFQA的影响. 不针对特定任务的调整,IFQA与所有三种对比属性产生负平均相关性,表明其现成的质量分数与本作中考虑的属性特定对比判断不直接一致. 精细地调整了相应的以人造人为主的说明,大大地改善了三个属性的性能. 在解释与拟议指标的比较时,这种区别很重要:我们的指标直接适用于真实的肖像,而不适合人造人或真实的肖像说明,而IFQA则受益于对人造人数据集的具体任务监督。 特别是微调后的改进,包括IFQA在整体对比方面的强效性能,提供了更多的证据,证明受控的"人造人"说明能捕捉到与对比相关的信息,这些信息会转移到真实的肖像上.
总体而言,这些结果支持了拟议中的"人造人"数据集,作为研究相片相貌对比的可控桥梁,同时也表明拟议中的"零镜头"度量标准有意义地概括到真实的肖像图像.

blocks.en: F.1 Face Cropping and Region Mask Extraction
blocks.zh: F.1 面部收割和地区面具提取

blocks.en:
We first detect the face region in each image to ensure that contrast analysis focuses solely on the face rather than the background.
For the face detection, we used the MTCNN implementation [ 77 ] provided by the facenet-pytorch library [ 15 ] . Each crop is resized to a fixed resolution of 585 × 820 585\times 820 pixels.
This step reduces variation in face scale and alignment and standardizes the image presentation for pairwise comparison experiments.
We then extract semantic facial regions using a BiSeNet face parsing model [ 76 , 75 ] , from which we derive three masks used throughout this work: a face mask for overall contrast, an eye mask for eye contrast, and a skin mask for micro-contrast as shown in Figure S3 .
blocks.zh:
我们首先检测每个图像中的相貌区域,以确保对比分析只注重相貌而不是背景.
为了进行面相检测,我们使用了由facenet-pytorch库提供的MTCNN执行[77]. [15]. 每种作物被调整为585×820 585\times 820像素的固定分辨率.
这一步骤减少了面相尺度和对齐的变异,并标准化了成对比较实验的图像演示.
然后我们用BiSeNet的面部剖析模型取出语义面部区域[76,75],我们从中得出了整个工作过程中所用的三个口罩:一个面罩用于整体对比,一个眼罩用于眼相对比,一个皮肤口罩用于微缩相容,如图S3所示。

blocks.en: The complete dataset contains images captured with 29 smartphones from multiple manufacturers, covering a broad range of device categories and ISP characteristics. Table S12 summarizes the device brands and models included in the dataset. The dataset contains two mannequin subjects, Eugene and Diana, and the processed comparison subsets are organized into five groups corresponding to different lighting regimes, as described in the main paper.

blocks.en: We evaluate the data under two complementary conditions. Within-lighting condition corresponds to a within-group device-disjoint split on Groups 1–4, while Mixed-lighting condition is a cross-group evaluation in which Groups 1–4 are used as the source set and Group 5 is used as the target set. The purpose of Within-lighting condition is to measure generalization across unseen devices within the same lighting regime, whereas Mixed-lighting condition evaluates transfer to a broader mixed group with more diverse contrast variation.
blocks.zh: 我们在两个互补条件下评估数据。 发光内条件相当于在1–4组上进行组内设备分拆,而混合发光条件则是一种跨组评价,其中1–4组作为源集,5组作为目标集. 照明内条件的目的是测量同一照明系统内未见设备的通用情况,而混合照明条件则评价向具有更多样化对比差异的更广泛的混合组的转移情况。

blocks.en: F.2.1 Within-lighting condition.
blocks.zh: F.2.1 照明内状况。

blocks.en:
This protocol is applied only to Groups 1–4. For each mannequin and each group, the split is performed by device rather than by image, so that the same smartphone never appears in both training and validation. This provides a strict device-disjoint evaluation setting and avoids optimistic correlations caused by device-specific ISP signatures appearing in both subsets.
Among the remaining samples, the validation devices are selected to satisfy three criteria: (i) strict device separation, (ii) a validation size close to the target ratio, and (iii) a reasonable balance between the training and validation subsets in JOD space. The balancing criterion uses the mean and standard deviation of the four annotation dimensions (Preference, Overall, Eye, and Micro) as a secondary constraint when constructing the split. This procedure yields a device-disjoint partition while keeping the train and validation subsets reasonably matched in perceptual-score distribution.
blocks.zh:
该议定书仅适用于第1至4组。 对每名模特和每组人来说,拆分是通过设备而不是由图像来完成的,这样同样的智能手机就不会在训练和验证中同时出现. 这提供了一个严格的设备分化评价设置,并避免了两个子集中出现的设备特定ISP签名所造成的乐观相关性.
在所余样本中,选取的验证装置要符合三个标准: (一)严格设备分离, (二)验证大小接近目标比例, (三)在JOD空间中训练与验证子集之间保持合理平衡. 平衡标准使用四个注释维度(偏好,整体,眼和微)的平均值和标准偏差作为构建分解时的次要约束. 这个程序产生一个设备分解分区,同时保持列车和验证子集在知觉分数分布上合理匹配.

blocks.en: F.2.2 Mixed-lighting condition.
blocks.zh: F.2.2 混合照明条件。

blocks.en: Mixed-lighting condition uses Groups 1–4 as the source set and Group 5 as the target set. As Group 5 is constructed by mixing samples from the other lighting groups, any duplicated samples from Groups 1–4 are excluded from the training set and removed from the released evaluation subset to avoid leakage across protocols. Group 5 provides a broader and more heterogeneous evaluation setting than Within-lighting condition . In this protocol, no additional train/validation split is performed within Group 5; instead, the goal is to measure how well a method transfers from the structured lighting conditions represented by Groups 1–4 to the more diverse contrast distribution represented by Group 5.
blocks.zh: 混合照明条件使用第1至第4组作为源集,第5组作为目标集. 由于第5组是通过混合其他照明组的样品来构建的,因此第1至4组的任何重复样品都被排除在培训单元之外,并被从释放的评价子集中取出,以避免跨协议渗出。 第5组提供比灯内条件更广泛、更多样的评价环境。 在本协议中,第5组内部没有进行额外的列车/验证分拆;相反,目标是衡量从第1至4组所代表的结构化照明条件到第5组所代表的更多样化对比分布的方法转移情况。

blocks.en: F.3 Annotation Consistency Analysis
blocks.zh: F.3 一致性分析

blocks.en:
We conducted two complementary analyses to assess the consistency of the collected annotations. First, we computed binary pairwise agreement as a direct measure on the raw pairwise decisions. The component-level tasks showed moderate agreement: eye contrast achieved 0.666 ± 0.101 0.666\pm 0.101 , micro-contrast 0.726 ± 0.092 0.726\pm 0.092 , and overall contrast 0.678 ± 0.106 0.678\pm 0.106 . Micro-contrast produced the highest agreement, consistent with the relatively direct judgment of fine-detail visibility. Balanced contrast showed lower agreement 0.588 ± 0.124 0.588\pm 0.124 , reflecting the more subjective nature of this holistic task.
Second, we also evaluated the stability of the recovered perceptual scales using a leave-one-observer-out analysis. For each task, we repeatedly removed one observer, recomputed the JOD scale from the remaining annotations, and measured its correlation with the JOD scale obtained from the full annotation set. The results are shown in Figure S15 . The resulting PLCC and SRCC values show that the inferred scales remain correlated after observer removal, especially for micro-contrast, which achieves the highest correlations under both evaluation settings. This indicates that the recovered JOD scales retain meaningful stability when individual observers are
excluded and can serve as perceptual references for metric validation.

blocks.en: Appendix G Pairwise Comparison Tool
blocks.zh: 附录 G 对等 比较工具

blocks.en:
During the experiments, the annotators performed pairwise comparisons using a custom annotation tool designed to present two images side by side and record their judgments for different perceptual attributes. For each comparison, the annotators selected the image that best matched the target criterion, depending on the annotation task. Figures S18 and S19 show example interfaces used for overall tonal contrast annotation. Figures S20 and S21 are for eye contrast annotation. Figures S22 and S23 illustrate example interfaces for micro-contrast annotation. Lastly, Figures S24 and S25 show example interfaces for balanced contrast annotation. Before the main experiment, all annotators were provided with detailed annotation guidelines and received two hours of prior training to ensure a consistent understanding of the evaluation criteria. Each annotation session took approximately one hour per attribute.
The total annotation time amounted to 160 hours across all annotations.

blocks.en: To illustrate the perceptual scales recovered from the pairwise annotations, we show example images sorted by their JOD values for each attribute. In all figures, the examples are ordered from lower to higher JOD. For overall contrast, eye contrast, and micro-contrast, higher JOD corresponds to more of the corresponding contrast attribute. For balanced contrast preference, higher JOD indicates a stronger human preference for the corresponding image. This ordering allows a visual inspection of how each recovered perceptual scale varies across the dataset. Figures S26 and S27 show overall contrast examples for Eugene and Diana. Figures S28 and S29 show eye-contrast examples. Figures S30 and S31 show micro-contrast examples. Finally, Figures S32 and S33 show examples sorted by balanced contrast preference JOD.
